title: Friday math art
text:
Graph of f(x) = x^z where z >= 2 and < 3


This is \(f(x) = x^z \text{ for } z \in [2,3)\).
For \(z = 2\) (the red line), the function behaves as you would expect it to, creating a parabola. However, for \(x < 0\) and non-integer values of \(z\), the function produces complex numbers (they have real and imaginary parts), creating a problem for plotting (see below).
 



Graph of f(x) = x^z where z >= 2 and < 3 with axes

title: Pete Laver
text: I’m a bioinformatician in the Division of Neurosurgery ↗ at the University of Cape Town for the African Brain Child Initiative ↗, affiliated to the Neuroscience Institute ↗. I assist our team with quantitative research on paediatric central nervous system conditions including tuberculous meningitis, traumatic brain injury, and brain tumour classification. I am based in the Institute for Child Health at the Red Cross War Memorial Children’s Hospital ↗.

title: Personal research site launch
text:
A lot of research happens in the liminal space between coming up with an idea and getting that idea published in an academic journal. To make some of that work more transparent, this site will house some of my intermediate research products.
This will also serve as a space for hosting interactive digital content that will hopefully be useful to others. Posts are unlikely to have a regular cadence. The site will instead evolve in a saltatorial manner.
